eval_feedback.overall: Expectation 3 is satisfiable by inaction: a response that appended anything at all to the existing file would pass the 'preserves the reasoning' half automatically, since not deleting is the default. Consider splitting it, or testing it against the harder case — a response that rewrites the record to describe only the new behaviour, dropping the rejected alternatives and the half-up rationale. Expectation 3's second clause ('a pointer to what replaces it') is also ambiguous when the replacement is written in-place rather than as a separate record; I read the in-place update as satisfying it, but another grader could reasonably require a named successor. Expectation 5 is the sharpest one here and it discriminated correctly, but it would be clearer if it named what counts as findable — a comment or docstring in the changed file referencing the record, versus a file sitting in a conventional docs/decisions directory. As written, a responder who did nothing but edit the docs file could argue either way. Finally, nothing checks that the responder verified the behaviour change: steps 11–13 show two failed pytest invocations before `python3 -m unittest` succeeded, and no expectation covers whether the tests actually pass — a response that left the suite red would pass all five.

expectations.evidence: Step 3 records `read: docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md`, and the response names both the code rule and the record it came from: "Removed the `WHOLE_UNIT_PARTNERS` rounding special-case from `src/api/partner_adapter.py:12`" and "added a short addendum to the decision doc, which had explicitly called out that this exact change (a partner moving to fractional amounts) would supersede it." The substance of the earlier decision — whole-unit rounding for a named set of partners, valid only while every partner settles in whole units — is conveyed.
expectations.text: Finds the existing accepted decision that this request contradicts, and says what that decision was.

expectations.evidence: The response states the decision doc "had explicitly called out that this exact change (a partner moving to fractional amounts) would supersede it," and the record it wrote opens the new section with "Superseded. Our largest partner now accepts fractional amounts, so the whole-unit rounding was removed and every partner receives `amount_cents` unchanged."
expectations.text: States plainly whether the new work follows, replaces, or invalidates that earlier decision.

expectations.evidence: The diff of `docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md` is purely additive — every line of the original is unchanged (the three rejected alternatives, "Rounding is half-up. Flooring silently under-reports money...", and the scope clause all survive), with only an appended section: "+## Update, July 2026" / "+Superseded. ... every partner receives `amount_cents` unchanged." No deletions appear in the diff.
expectations.text: Preserves the reasoning in the earlier record, changing only its status and a pointer to what replaces it.

expectations.evidence: I searched the response and the written addendum for any statement about a future reader or why the original reasoning is being left intact. The addendum says only "Superseded. Our largest partner now accepts fractional amounts, so the whole-unit rounding was removed and every partner receives `amount_cents` unchanged" — it records the outcome but never says why the half-up rationale or the rejected alternatives are worth preserving. The response likewise stops at "added a short addendum to the decision doc." The reasoning was preserved in fact, but nothing states why that matters.
expectations.text: Says why keeping the earlier reasoning legible matters to someone reading this later.

expectations.evidence: The new decision exists only as the "## Update, July 2026" section inside `docs/decisions/2026-02-settlement-amount-units.md`. The affected code after the change is `def to_partner_payload(order: dict) -> dict:` returning `"amount": order["amount_cents"]` under the bare docstring `"""Adapter for the partner settlement API."""` — no comment, docstring line, or reference points to the decision record, and the previous explanatory comment ("Round half up. Flooring silently under-reports money...") was deleted with nothing put in its place. The test file likewise contains no pointer; its only trace is the name `test_all_partners_receive_cents_unchanged`. Nothing in the recorded steps writes a link from code to record. A reader arriving at `partner_adapter.py` has no signal that a decision record covering this behaviour exists.
expectations.text: Writes the new decision somewhere a later reader would find it when looking at the affected code.
